project.feature: A 21-second 9:16 app film: split a group dinner bill from one receipt photo.

summary.tone: Warm, quick and a little funny.
summary.message: Crumb turns one restaurant receipt into everyone's fair share in three taps.
summary.arc: Hook → scan → claim → split → settle → logo

options.name: Diner receipt
options.pitch: Warm receipt paper, ink and one tomato-red accent. Feels like the table you just ate at.
options.why: The product starts from a paper receipt; the look carries that object through the whole film.
options.tradeoff: Quieter on a busy feed than C.

options.name: Midnight ledger
options.pitch: Deep navy, warm amber, crisp geometric type. Late dinner, serious money.
options.why: Signals trust for a payments feature.
options.tradeoff: Less playful; the paper receipt is the only warm surface.

options.name: Citrus pop
options.pitch: Tangerine field, white UI, electric-blue accent, chunky grotesque. Loud and friendly.
options.why: Stops the scroll in a 9:16 feed.
options.tradeoff: Risks feeling like a generic consumer-app ad.

options.name: Bell Beats
options.why: Quiet first bar, then the beat drops at 2.0 s, right where the total lands. Playful bells suit a dinner app. Measured 120 BPM (librosa says 96).

options.name: Tropicorp Advertisement
options.why: Bright, steady corporate pulse; safest under the voice, but generic. Measured 102 BPM.

options.name: Wet Square Techno Beat
options.why: Driving techno with a strong kick; energetic, but it fights a soft voice and a warm look. Measured 127 BPM.

options.name: Weighted spring
options.why: About 2.5 % overshoot on UI pieces, none on type: things land with weight.

options.name: Crisp (power3)
options.why: Clean decelerations, no overshoot; calmer and more corporate.

options.name: Snappy (power5)
options.why: Fast starts and hard stops; energetic, can feel mechanical.

options.name: Tight · 18.9 s
options.why: Every scene 10 % shorter; the voice lines get tight.

options.name: Standard · 21.0 s
options.why: Hits land on the 120 BPM grid at this pace.

options.name: Relaxed · 23.5 s
options.why: More air for reading; hits drift off the beat grid.

options.name: Sarah
options.intro: Fish Audio official voice. Young, soft and sincere, close to the mic. Our default narrator.
options.why: Soft and sincere; the house narrator. Sits well under a warm look.
options.lic: Fish Audio s2.1-pro-free output (commercial use allowed)

options.name: Calm Indian English
options.intro: Calm, clear and professional with an Indian accent.
options.why: Calm Indian English; closer to an Indian audience while staying in English.
options.lic: Fish Audio s2.1-pro-free output (commercial use allowed)
options.needs: voice takes: run voices/make_voices.sh with your own Fish key

options.name: Hindi, bright
options.intro: Young, bright and confident Hindi voice; energetic and clear.
options.why: The whole film in Hindi with a bright young voice. On-screen text stays English.

engine.name: HyperFrames 0.8.134
engine.why: Code-drawn phone UI, kinetic type and one seekable GSAP timeline; matches the installed Claude plugin; 0 ms audio lag measured on 2026-10-06.
engine.alt: bang-motion 1.19.0 (same GSAP stack, one index.html) or video-shotcraft (when a real product with real screens exists).

references.name: brag-slim launch videos (_kits/brag, MIT)
references.borrow: entry → key action → result; the hook in two seconds; every frame postable
references.avoid: confetti, synth chimes, the Kokoro voice

references.name: Showreel gist, mobile mode (mirzemehdi)
references.borrow: code-drawn phone, touch ring with a press, screen pushes, cards lifting out of the phone
references.avoid: particle bursts, camera shake, a synthesized score

references.name: Our 010 MIRA
references.borrow: one object carried through every boundary; the accent lands inside the logo
references.avoid: a dark, slow opening; flat cards with no depth

style_rules.Colour: From the direction tokens only: one accent; text on the stage uses on-bg, inside the phone on-card.
style_rules.Type: One display face, one UI face, mono for money. At most two text levels; captions ≥ 5 % and UI ≥ 3 % of frame height after the camera push.
style_rules.Shape: Phone 780 × 1500, 108 px radius; pills and avatars round; cards 30 px radius.
style_rules.Motion: Springs with weight, overlap and follow-through; overshoot ≤ 4 % on UI, never on type; no pure opacity fades in production.
style_rules.Camera: Steady on UI; pushes land and stop; no handheld shake.
style_rules.Sound: Recorded foley only, fewer sounds than beats, airy whooshes, the logo landing is the loudest moment.

audio_notes: The voice leads; the bed ducks about 8 dB under each line (you hear this live here).
Final mix: −14 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1 dBTP, checked by cross-correlation and on an SFX-only stem.
The final adds a Mixkit low impact under the icon landing and one shimmer tail; both are render-only, so this page cannot play them.

qa.text: Crumb, Nonna's and the seven names are made up; check the name before any public post.
Previs fidelity: layout and motion are rough; type polish, masks and depth happen in production.
Fonts load from Google here; the HyperFrames build vendors them as local woff2 files.

versions.note: First previs: three directions, three beds, three motion feels, three pacings, three options on every scene decision.
Self-check fixes before your review: the hook reads from frame 0, and the wordmark fits the frame in every look.
Option libraries: 8 more looks, 11 more music beds, 7 motion feels, camera moves, transitions and a voice library (English and Hindi). Ask the director can add any of them.
Hook headline now reads "Seven friends. One receipt."
Seven friends everywhere: new voice takes for three lines in all 10 voices, a seventh diner (Ravi), seven amounts and six request cards.

chief.objective: Show in 21 seconds that one receipt photo becomes everyone's fair share.
chief.thesis: The receipt is the hero object: it is carried from paper into the phone and ends as the logo's promise.
chief.depth: Small product film: one combined approval gate instead of five, ten specialists active, four not needed.

story.viewer: Seven people, one long bill: who pays what?
Crumb can read the receipt from a photo.
Claiming dishes is a tap per name.
Everyone's share, tax and tip included, adds up.
Money requests go out in one tap and come back paid.

directors.name: Story director
directors.summary: Hook → discovery → proof → payoff → resolution → name. One idea per shot; the receipt connects them.
directors.why: A bill-splitting app is understood fastest as before and after: one bill, then seven fair shares.

directors.name: Script and voice director
directors.summary: Six short lines for Sarah, three wordings each, at most 3.4 words a second; the last line is also the tagline.
directors.why: Short lines leave room for the taps and sounds to be heard.

directors.name: Editorial director
directors.summary: Shots of 3.0 to 4.5 s; cuts on the beat only for the two hits (total and logo); the longest shot is the key action.
directors.why: Varying shot length and saving the beat for big moments keeps it from feeling like a music video.

directors.name: Art director
directors.summary: Three looks: diner receipt (recommended), midnight ledger, citrus pop.
directors.why: The paper receipt is the product's own starting point, so the recommended look grows out of it.

directors.name: Design and styleframe director
directors.summary: One accent colour, a code-drawn phone, money in a mono face, two text levels at most.
directors.why: Premium means subtracting: no decorative cards or borders.

directors.name: Typography director
directors.summary: One display face per look, one UI face, mono for amounts; headline 108 px, UI text at least 3 % of the frame after the push-in.
directors.why: It has to read on a phone held at arm's length.

directors.name: Reference director
directors.summary: brag-slim launch videos, the showreel gist's phone mode, our own 010 MIRA. Grammar only, never content.
directors.why: Each reference lends one principle; see the list for what we avoid.

directors.name: Camera director
directors.summary: Steady on UI, slow pushes to make text readable, a locked frame for the logo.
directors.why: Product films keep the camera calm; each move has a reason written on the shot.

directors.name: Motion director
directors.summary: Weighted springs with about 2.5 % overshoot on UI, none on type; the finger presses before anything reacts.
directors.why: Cause before effect is what makes UI motion believable.

directors.name: Transition director
directors.summary: Receipt zooms into the viewfinder, screens slide, a hard cut resets for the payoff, the phone collapses into the icon.
directors.why: Every boundary carries something across; a cut is used where a reset helps.

directors.name: Music director
directors.summary: Bell Beats at a measured 120 BPM: quiet first bar, drop at 2.0 s on the total, the logo on the bar at 18.0 s.
directors.why: The track's own structure gives the two hits; we cut on phrases, not every beat.

directors.name: Sound design director
directors.summary: Recorded foley only: paper, touch taps, a soft whoosh per move, a riser into the logo, one landing.
directors.why: Real sounds for real actions; fewer sounds than beats.

directors.name: Mix director
directors.summary: Voice leads; music ducks about 8 dB under each line; the logo landing is the loudest moment; master −14 LUFS.
directors.why: A non-expert hears the words first and feels the landing.

directors.name: Asset director
directors.summary: Everything is drawn in code or recorded CC0 audio; no screenshots exist because Crumb is made up.
directors.why: See the asset list for each item's source and licence.

directors.name: Engine director
directors.summary: HyperFrames 0.8.134 for every shot (one film, one engine).
directors.why: Code-drawn UI and type on one seekable timeline; 0 ms audio lag measured.

directors.name: Pipeline director
directors.summary: After approval: freeze the spec, build shot by shot with stills, one render, self-check (your call for this sample).
directors.why: No renders until you approve; one worker, no parallel renders.

directors.name: QA director
directors.summary: Checks timing, beat hits, voice speed, text levels and product truth for your current picks.
directors.why: Issues are cheapest to fix here, before any render.

directors.name: VFX and compositing director
directors.summary: Not used.
directors.why: No footage to composite; house rules ban glows and particles anyway.

directors.name: Lighting director
directors.summary: Not used.
directors.why: Flat 2D UI film; no 3D scene to light.

directors.name: B-roll and caption director
directors.summary: Not used.
directors.why: No talking head or footage; the voice lines are short.

directors.name: Colour grading director
directors.summary: Not used.
directors.why: Colours come straight from the chosen look's tokens.

direction.name: Sober slate
direction.pitch: Cool grey ground, white cards and one steel-blue accent. Quiet and grown-up.
direction.why: The most restrained option: the product and the voice do all the talking.
direction.tradeoff: Can feel like any fintech app.

direction.name: Ocean calm
direction.pitch: Pale sky ground, navy type and a clear blue accent. Calm and trustworthy.
direction.why: Blue reads as safe money; soft ground keeps it friendly.
direction.tradeoff: Blue is the most common fintech colour.

direction.name: Paper mono
direction.pitch: Pure white, black ink, no colour at all. Editorial and exact.
direction.why: Lets the receipt itself be the hero; very premium when the type is right.
direction.tradeoff: No accent means hits need motion to read.

direction.name: Forest bistro
direction.pitch: Deep green, cream paper and a mustard accent. A good restaurant at night.
direction.why: Ties the app to eating out; warm and premium.
direction.tradeoff: Darker ground; small UI text needs the camera push.

direction.name: Terracotta
direction.pitch: Burnt orange ground, cream cards, espresso ink. Sunny trattoria.
direction.why: Warmer and more human than Citrus pop, still bold in a feed.
direction.tradeoff: Orange grounds are loud next to food photos.

direction.name: Mint fresh
direction.pitch: Mint ground, white cards, green accent. Light and easy.
direction.why: Feels like money that is sorted; fresh without shouting.
direction.tradeoff: Green can read as a bank.

direction.name: Plum night
direction.pitch: Plum ground, near-white cards and a pink accent. Bold and a little fun.
direction.why: Stands out at night in a feed; playful for a friends app.

direction.name: Butter and ink
direction.pitch: Butter-yellow ground, black ink, chunky grotesque. Cheerful and loud.
direction.why: Yellow is the friendliest colour in a feed; black keeps it graphic.

music.name: Calming piano loop
music.why: Solo piano at 60 BPM. The most sober option: nothing competes with the voice.
music.tradeoff: Little drive; the logo landing leans on the sound effects.

music.name: Calm background
music.why: Soft pads with a light pulse. Reads as a quiet, polished product film.
music.tradeoff: A weak beat, so hits land on the music's pulse less clearly.

music.name: Chill lo-fi e-piano
music.why: Warm lo-fi keys at 80 BPM. Feels like a late, relaxed dinner.
music.tradeoff: Loops every 24 s; a little sleepy for a call to action.

music.name: Chill background
music.why: Relaxed modern groove with a soft beat. Easy under a voice.
music.tradeoff: Fairly anonymous; less personality than the recommended bed.

music.name: Simple relaxing guitar
music.why: One acoustic guitar. Human and warm, fits a restaurant table.
music.tradeoff: No drums, so the beat grid is soft.

music.name: Blue sky ukulele
music.why: Bright ukulele and a happy lift. Friendly and casual.
music.tradeoff: Can feel like a stock ad if overused.

music.name: Little happy tune
music.why: Light, playful melody at 120 BPM: the same grid as the recommended bed.
music.tradeoff: Busy melody; it may fight the voice in shot 3.

music.name: Happy hip hop beat
music.why: Confident head-nod groove. Strong beats for the taps and the logo.
music.tradeoff: Heavier drums; keep the voice well above it.

music.name: Funky groove
music.why: Funky bass and drums. Fun and lively.
music.tradeoff: Swingy feel; hits sit less tightly on the grid.

music.name: Beach dance
music.why: Bright dance track at 120 BPM. Maximum energy.
music.tradeoff: Loud and busy; the least premium option.

music.name: Slow cinematic
music.why: Slow, emotional swells. Turns the film into a short story.
music.tradeoff: No steady beat, so nothing snaps to a grid; feels heavy for a bill-splitting app.

motion.name: Gentle (sine)
motion.why: Soft, even arrivals; nothing snaps. The calmest feel.

motion.name: Smooth (power2)
motion.why: A gentle deceleration; softer than Crisp.

motion.name: Fast-out (expo)
motion.why: Moves almost instantly, then glides in. Modern app feel.

motion.name: Soft spring
motion.why: A rounder spring with about 1 % overshoot; friendly but calm.

motion.name: Playful pop
motion.why: Visible bounce on arrival (about 8 %). Fun, but above the 4 % house limit for UI.
motion.tradeoff: Breaks the house overshoot rule; use only for a playful brand.

motion.name: Slow cinematic
motion.why: Slow in, slow out. Weighty and deliberate.

motion.name: Mechanical (linear)
motion.why: Constant speed, robotic. Useful only as a contrast.

pacing.name: Very tight · 16.8 s
pacing.why: Every shot 20 % shorter. Punchy for a feed; the voice must be quick.

pacing.name: Easy · 22.1 s
pacing.why: A little more air between beats.

pacing.name: Slow · 26.3 s
pacing.why: Very relaxed; hits drift off the beat grid.

camera.name: Locked
camera.why: No camera move: the content moves, the frame stays still.

camera.name: Slow push
camera.why: A gentle push draws the eye in.

camera.name: Strong push
camera.why: A clear push in; good for making small text readable.

camera.name: Pull back
camera.why: Starts close, opens out to reveal the whole frame.

camera.name: Drift left
camera.why: A slow sideways drift; adds life to a hold.

camera.name: Drift up
camera.why: A slow rise; reads top to bottom content.

transition.name: Hard cut
transition.why: Instant change. Clean, but nothing carries across.

transition.name: Push up
transition.why: The new shot pushes the old one up and away.

transition.name: Slide left
transition.why: Like moving to the next app screen.

transition.name: Quick slide
transition.why: A faster slide that feels snappy.

transition.name: Zoom through
transition.why: Push through the frame into the next shot.

transition.name: Iris from centre
transition.why: The next shot opens out of the middle.
